items.definition:
forbid
Smoking is prohibited in this area.

enlist
The company plans to recruit new staff next month.

force or oblige (someone) to do something
The law will compel employers to provide health insurance.

produce (a book, list, or other publication) by assembling information
She needs to compile a report by Friday.

to suggest without stating directly
His silence seemed to imply agreement.

to control or maintain the rate or speed of
The government regulates the banking industry.

to walk with difficulty through water or mud
We had to wade through the shallow river.

express complete disapproval of
The government condemned the terrorist attack.

to throw in different directions
The wind scattered the leaves across the yard.

to manage or supervise
The government will administer the new program.

to compel observance of or compliance with (a law, rule, or obligation)
The police are here to enforce the law.

to abduct (someone) and hold them captive
The criminals tried to kidnap the wealthy businessman.

go on a long arduous journey
They decided to trek across the mountains.

to ease pain or distress; to replace
The medicine will relieve your headache.

to reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it
She used a machine to grind the coffee beans.

cause (someone) to feel a sudden wave of excitement and pleasure
The roller coaster ride thrilled the children.

make sure or demonstrate that (something) is true, accurate, or justified
Please verify your account details.

to happen; to emerge
New problems often arise when we try to implement complex solutions.

to release; to send out; to fulfill (a duty)
The hospital will discharge the patient tomorrow.

to make a hole in something with a sharp object
She decided to pierce her ears.

to be greater than or go beyond (a limit, amount, etc.)
Do not exceed the speed limit.

to deny (someone) access to or membership of a place, group, or area
The club decided to exclude members who didn't pay their fees.

to explain the meaning of (information, words, or actions)
It's difficult to interpret these complex instructions.

to make something operate automatically
We need to automate this process to save time.

receive (money, property, or a title) as an heir
She will inherit a large fortune from her grandmother.

(of a medical practitioner) advise and authorize the use of (a medicine or treatment) for someone
The doctor prescribed antibiotics for her infection.

break or fail to comply with
He was accused of violating the law.

to cause (someone) to have a wrong idea or impression about someone or something
Don't let appearances mislead you.

to make a choice from a range of possibilities
You can opt to pay monthly or annually.

to build (something) again after it has been damaged or destroyed
They plan to rebuild the old house.

to thrust a knife or other pointed weapon into someone or something
He tried to stab the attacker with a pen.

to fix something firmly in a surrounding mass
The journalist was embedded with the troops.

consist of; be made up of
The committee will comprise members from various departments.

prevent (a process or activity) from continuing or being carried out properly
Don't interfere in matters that don't concern you.

to cause or bring about
His question prompted a long discussion.

to become or cause to become incorporated into a liquid so as to form a solution
Sugar dissolves quickly in hot water.

(of a ghost) manifest itself in (a place) regularly
The old house is said to be haunted by a friendly ghost.

revoke or annul (a law or act)
The government decided to repeal the controversial law.

cause (something) to pass on from one place or person to another
The radio tower transmits signals across the region.

make or become united, uniform, or whole
The goal is to unify the different departments.

put at risk
Pollution can endanger wildlife.

achieve or realize
He worked hard to fulfill his dreams.

to entice or allure someone to do something
The delicious smell of cookies tempted me.

destroy or ruin (something); cause (someone) severe and overwhelming shock or grief
The news of her death devastated her family.

construct (a building, monument, or other structure); set up
They plan to erect a new monument in the town square.

to make fun of someone or something
Don't mock his efforts; he's trying his best.

to depict or represent (someone or something) in a work of art or literature
The artist tried to portray the beauty of the landscape.

to commit oneself to and begin (an enterprise or responsibility)
The company decided to undertake a new project.

meet (someone) face to face with hostile or argumentative intent
She decided to confront her fears.

make (secret or new information) known
The company refused to disclose the financial details.

to give evidence as a witness
He was called to testify in court.

to allow the existence of something without interference
I cannot tolerate such rude behavior.

distribute (resources or duties) for a particular purpose
The government decided to allocate more funds to education.

make (an idea, impression, or feeling) known or understandable to someone
His words failed to convey his true feelings.

to improve by making small changes
We need to refine our strategy.

strengthen
The new evidence will reinforce our argument.

make practical and effective use of
We should utilize all available resources.

cause (someone) to become dependent on a particular substance or activity
He was addicted to gambling.

restrict (a person or thing) to a limited space or area
The patient was confined to bed.

combine; strengthen
The companies decided to consolidate their resources.

suffer patiently; last over a period of time
She had to endure a lot of pain during her recovery.

fail to notice or ignore
Please don't overlook the details.

to strike hard; to criticize harshly
He tried to bash the door open.

to hold or keep someone in official custody; to delay
The police decided to detain the suspect for questioning.
